b.answer:
Worked example: Glow Studio, a fictional salon chain in Enugu (3 branches) selling bridal packages and memberships. Interviewed: the owner and the senior stylist who books bridal clients.

Last won deal: Instagram DM → price list sent on WhatsApp → trial session booked by phone → deposit by transfer → wedding day → balance paid.

LaneSteps
ReceptionistReads DMs, sends price list
Senior stylistBooks trial, quotes package, takes deposit
OwnerApproves discounts, checks transfers

Leaks → requirements

  1. DMs after 7 p.m. wait until morning → every enquiry acknowledged within 5 minutes and owned within 1 working hour.
  2. Trial bookings live in the stylist's phone → every trial is a dated activity the team can see.
  3. No one chases brides who got the price list but didn't book → a follow-up task 2 days after the price list.

The stylist read the map and said: "Yes, but add that brides often message my personal number." Added.
mistakes: Interviewing only the owner, so the map shows the imagined process.
Leaks written as complaints ("staff are slow") instead of requirements.
Fewer than three leaks, or leaks with no requirement.
b.pass: A swimlane map with roles, steps and hand-overs, at least three leaks, each rewritten as a measurable requirement, and the interviewee's confirmation that it matches reality.
b.redo: Send it back if it maps only one person's view, leaks are not turned into requirements, or there's no sign the interviewee checked it.

s.answer:
Worked example: Glow Studio (fictional, Enugu). Requirements document, 6 pages.

Goals and success measures: median first reply to enquiries under 10 minutes in opening hours (now about 3 hours); 100% of trials with a follow-up task; bridal conversion from trial to deposit visible monthly; owner stops counting deposits in a notebook.

MoSCoW (14 items): 6 must (capture DMs/WhatsApp/web enquiries; owner per enquiry; trials as activities; deposit status on deal; branch permissions; monthly dashboard), 4 should (follow-up tasks; birthday offers to consented members), 2 could (membership renewals; stylist commission report), 2 won't (custom app; stock management).

Data audit · 3 sheets · 2,640 rows
Duplicates (phone) ............ 710 (27%)
No phone ....................... 95
Active last 18 months .......... 1,320
Decision: migrate 1,320 people + 41 open bridal deals; archive rest

Out of scope: stock, payroll, commission. Risks: stylists using personal WhatsApp; owner availability for sign-off.
mistakes: More than half the requirements marked must.
Success measures that can't be counted ("better service").
A data audit that gives row totals but no duplicates or active count.
s.pass: Goals with numeric success measures, a process map, MoSCoW requirements with musts at most half, a data audit counting duplicates and active records, and an out-of-scope list.
s.redo: Send it back if success measures aren't numbers, every item is a must, or the data audit is missing duplicates and inactive rows.

g.answer:
Worked example of the evidence to submit (names removed): "Client A, logistics company, Lagos, 6 sales staff".

  • Workshop 1 (90 min): owner, 2 sales reps, dispatcher; photographed sticky-note wall; 2 won and 1 lost deal walked.
  • Workshop 2 (60 min): map played back; 3 corrections recorded.

Recommendation: Zoho CRM Professional for 6 users (Blueprint for the quote-approval process was a must), priced for 12 months from the vendor's page on the day, date written; compared with HubSpot Sales Hub Professional.

Sign-off · Requirements v1.1
Reviewed by: Operations Director · Date: 2026-11-14
Changes requested: 2 (both applied) · Status: approved

Submit: the redacted document, workshop photos with faces removed, and the sign-off note.
mistakes: Price quoted without the date it was checked.
Workshops with only management in the room.
No written approval or review from the client.
g.pass: Evidence of two workshops with the people who do the work, a complete requirements document with a dated platform and plan recommendation, and the client's sign-off or formal review.
g.redo: Send it back if there's no evidence a real client reviewed it, the platform choice isn't tied to must-haves, or personal data isn't removed.
